articles.title: Dhamaal 4 Just Opened to ₹12 Crore. But the Real Show Was the Ghost Who Came Back.
articles.excerpt: Satish Kaushik’s digital resurrection as Bata Bhai opens the franchise’s biggest box office day in seven years — and the diaspora is eating it up from Sydney to New Jersey.
articles.image_caption: Ajay Devgn, the lead of the Dhamaal franchise (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dhanush and Vetri Maaran Just Dropped a First Look. It’s Not Vada Chennai 2.
articles.excerpt: The most decorated duo in Tamil cinema abandons the gangster playbook for a full-blown ancient warrior epic — and hands the music to the kid behind Katchi Sera.
articles.image_caption: Dhanush, who stars as the warrior king in Thamizh Murugan (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ranveer Singh Just Took India's Biggest Film to Japan. The Numbers Are Obscene.
articles.excerpt: Dhurandhar opens in Tokyo today with a ₹3,100 crore franchise behind it — and Saif Ali Khan just declared there's a 'before and after Dhurandhar' era in Bollywood.
articles.image_caption: Ranveer Singh at a promotional event for Dhurandhar (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Priyanka Chopra FaceTimed Nick Jonas from Wimbledon's Royal Box. The Internet Lost It.
articles.excerpt: Fresh off Paris Couture Week in Dior florals, Bollywood's most global star showed up at the All England Club in all white — and made a phone call that broke the internet.
articles.image_caption: Priyanka Chopra Jonas at a red carpet event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Four Stars. One Husband. Zero Sense. Pati Patni Aur Woh Do Just Landed on Netflix.
articles.excerpt: Ayushmann Khurrana's comedy of errors — with Sara Ali Khan, Rakul Preet Singh, and Wamiqa Gabbi all in the mix — finally arrives for the diaspora after a solid theatrical run.
articles.image_caption: Ayushmann Khurrana at a film event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: What to Watch This Week: Netflix Drops a Triple Bomb, SonyLIV Brings the Grit, and Dhamaal Returns to Theatres
articles.excerpt: From a courtroom reunion thirty years in the making to a three-hour Telugu epic and a Tamil murder mystery, this week’s streaming lineup is absurdly stacked. Here are our picks.
articles.image_caption: Sunny Deol, star of Ikka, this week's top streaming pick (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ram Charan's Peddi Just Landed on Netflix. Here's Why the Diaspora Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: After a ₹340 crore theatrical run that dominated Andhra Pradesh but stumbled everywhere else, the three-hour Telugu sports epic gets its second chance — and for NRIs who missed it in cinemas, this is the version that matters.
articles.image_caption: Ram Charan at a promotional event (Wikipedia)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: They Took Satluj Off the Internet. Now Gurudwaras Are Screening It Across Five States.
articles.excerpt: Diljit Dosanjh's film about murdered human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra lasted 48 hours on ZEE5 before it was pulled. The Sikh community's response has been to open its doors wider.
articles.image_caption: Diljit Dosanjh at a public event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Somebody Said King Costs ₹450 Crore. Siddharth Anand Had One Word.
articles.excerpt: Bollywood Hungama dropped the number. The director posted 'FALSE' on X. But with Suhana Khan's debut, Abhishek Bachchan as the villain, and 150 days of global shooting — whatever King actually costs, it's clearly everything Shah Rukh Khan has.
articles.image_caption: Shah Rukh Khan at a promotional event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: No Heroine. A Bald Akshay. Priyamani as the Villain. Golmaal FIVE Is Breaking Every Rule the Franchise Ever Had.
articles.excerpt: Rohit Shetty's fifth instalment drops the love interest entirely, brings back Sharman Joshi after twenty years, and turns The Family Man's star into the comedy's central antagonist — all for the franchise's 20th anniversary in early 2027.
articles.image_caption: Ajay Devgn at a film event (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Date Is Set. Ramayana Drops Its First Trailer July 18 — at India's Grandest Stage.
articles.excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's ₹4,000-crore epic will unveil its official trailer at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, with Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and a dream cast expected on stage.
articles.image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor, who plays Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hrithik Roshan Has No Film in 2026. He's Never Been More in Demand.
articles.excerpt: The Chhaava director just pitched him a script. Rajinikanth already shot with him. Krrish 4 is quietly coming alive. And Hombale wants to build an empire around him.
articles.image_caption: Hrithik Roshan at a public appearance (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sunny Deol Has Never Made a Netflix Film. Akshaye Khanna Hasn't Faced Him in Thirty Years. That Changes Thursday.
articles.excerpt: Ikka reunites two of Bollywood's most magnetic actors in a courtroom thriller that asks what happens when the best lawyer in the country is forced to defend a man he knows is guilty. Streaming globally on Netflix, July 10.
articles.image_caption: Sunny Deol stars in Ikka, his Netflix debut (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: She Left Toronto With Nothing. She Came Back to Sing at the World Cup.
articles.excerpt: Nora Fatehi became the first Bollywood performer to headline a FIFA World Cup opening ceremony, debuted on NBC's TODAY show, and made Indian fans in Dallas cry by just being herself. The most Googled Bollywood artist in the world right now is a Moroccan-Canadian who learned Hindi in her twenties.
articles.image_caption: Nora Fatehi, the first Bollywood performer at a FIFA World Cup opening ceremony (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Every Critic Just Said the Same Word About The Odyssey. The Word Is 'Masterpiece.'
articles.excerpt: The Odyssey premiered in London to the most ecstatic reviews of Nolan's career. One performance drew a comparison to Heath Ledger's Joker — and a British-Indian actor nobody saw coming just became the film's quiet MVP.
articles.image_caption: Christopher Nolan, whose latest film The Odyssey is being hailed as his masterpiece (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Her Twins Read the Divorce Papers in German. Her Husband Said, 'I'll Get You a Job Cleaning Supermarkets.' Celina Jaitly Is Done Being Quiet.
articles.excerpt: In a raw, devastating interview, the former Miss India reveals the full scope of her cross-border divorce nightmare — the ₹20 crore she says she lost, the custody battle she's fighting across two countries, and the one Bollywood friend who never left her side.
articles.image_caption: Celina Jaitly at a promotional event in Mumbai
